tracks.title: Your Side of the Duvet
tracks.subject: a man in Leeds whose wife rolls the whole duvet around herself every night; he buys a second duvet just for himself, and every morning she is under his one anyway
tracks.caption: Raspy blue-eyed soul pop, mid-2020s radio ballad style. Rhodes electric piano holding slow gospel-tinged chords, an upright piano doubling the hook, fingerstyle electric bass, a brushed drum kit with a soft backbeat, Hammond organ swells under the choruses. Warm live-room mix with light tape saturation and a close vocal. Male baritone with a gritty raspy belt, hushed verses rising to full-chest choruses. 74 BPM, E-flat major. Tender, warm and quietly amused. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM drop, no gospel choir takeover, no country twang.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes and brushed kit]

[Verse 1]
Three a.m., the window's open wide
You roll over and pull it to your side
Wrapped up like a sausage roll in white
I'm on the edge in my socks all night

[Pre-Chorus]
I could wake you, I could pull it back
But your face is doing that

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take my side too
I'll freeze till Monday, darling
If it's keeping you

[Verse 2]
So I bought my own, a single, navy blue
Twenty quid from Dunelm, brand new
Folded neat beside you on the bed
Morning comes, it's round your head

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take the navy too
I'll buy a third one, darling
And you'll take that too

[Bridge - organ swell]
Cold feet on my knees
That's the deal, I guess

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take my side too
I'll freeze for twenty winters
If I'm next to you

[Outro - Rhodes alone]
Three a.m., the window's open wide
Keep it, love, I'm fine

tracks.title: Thursday, Says Dave
tracks.subject: a man in a Salford terrace whose bathroom tap drips all week while the plumber Dave keeps texting 'Thursday', until he starts dancing round the flat to the drip
tracks.caption: Madchester baggy revival, late-80s Manchester indie-dance style. A shuffling funky-drummer breakbeat with maracas and tambourine, chiming wah-wah rhythm guitar, a high melodic bass line carrying the hook, a Hammond organ comping on the offbeats. Hazy baggy mix, reverb on the guitars, loose swaying groove. Male lead in a laconic Mancunian half-sung drawl, a few lads joining the chorus. 98 BPM, A major. Sunny, loose and mock-patient. No britpop stadium anthem, no autotune, no trap drums, no EDM drop, no metal distortion.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - breakbeat, wah guitar and bass]

[Verse 1]
Bathroom tap goes drip all night
Tried a spanner, no dice
Rang the plumber, he's called Dave
Dave says Thursday, Dave's a saint

[Pre-Chorus]
Monday, Tuesday, still it goes
Drip drip drip, the bucket knows

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Thursday, he swears
Bucket in the bath
And I'm dancing on the stairs

[Verse 2]
Got a rhythm, got a beat
Drip goes kick and I move my feet
Tea towel round my head like a hat
Next door's cat just stares at that

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Which Thursday, mate?
Bucket's nearly full
And I'm grooving while I wait

[Bridge - organ and maracas]
Washer costs a quid
Dave's van is in Rhyl

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Here he comes at last
Two minutes with a washer
Now the party's in the past

[Outro - breakbeat fades]
Quiet in the bathroom now
Kind of miss it anyhow

tracks.title: Day Three Hundred Sixty-Six
tracks.subject: a man whose kettle dies on day 366 of its one-year warranty, who storms the electrical shop with the receipt and a calendar, and is offered ten percent off a new kettle
tracks.caption: Bay Area thrash metal, mid-80s style. Two palm-muted downpicked electric guitars playing fast chugging riffs, an overdriven bass locked to them, galloping double-kick drums with a cracking snare, one short shredded guitar solo. Tight dry 80s thrash production with scooped mids. Male lead in a barked mid-range thrash shout with clear diction, gang shouts on the hook. 184 BPM, E minor. Furious, ridiculous and righteous. No nu-metal rap, no deathcore growls or breakdowns, no autotune, no pop chorus, no symphonic keys.

[Intro - galloping riff and double kick]

[Verse 1]
Morning brew, I flick the switch
Not a spark and not a hiss
Turn the box, the sticker reads
One year cover, guaranteed

[Pre-Chorus]
Count the days on the calendar
Three six six, one day too far

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Kettle dead and nothing fixed
Day three hundred sixty-six
Leap year, mate, I know your tricks

[Verse 2]
Down the high street, receipt in hand
Kettle tucked beneath my arm
Lad in blue just shakes his head
Should have died a day ahead

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Policy says no to this
Day three hundred sixty-six
Small print says you take the hit

[Bridge - guitar solo]

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Ten percent off, that's the fix
Day three hundred sixty-six
Boil it in a pan, that's it

[Outro - final riff and stop]
New kettle, same brand, same shop
Mark the date and watch the clock

tracks.title: Somebody Else's List
tracks.subject: a woman who finds a stranger's handwritten shopping list in the pocket of a charity-shop wool coat, buys every item on it and cooks whatever that list was meant to become
tracks.caption: Sophisti-pop, late-80s British style. A singing fretless bass, muted jazz guitar chords with a chorus effect, soprano saxophone answering the vocal, a DX7-style electric piano, soft programmed drums with a live hi-hat. Glossy polished mix with gentle room reverb. Female alto, smooth and conversational, close-mic, light double-tracking on the chorus. 96 BPM, D major. Wistful, curious and quietly charmed. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM drop, no rock distortion, no jazz scat.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - fretless bass and soprano sax]

[Verse 1]
Camel coat from the charity shop
Twelve pounds and it fit
Left-hand pocket, folded twice
A list in someone's script

[Pre-Chorus]
Leeks, two lemons, crème fraîche
Thyme, and don't forget the bread

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's night
I'm filling up my basket
With the things you chose to write

[Verse 2]
Mussels, butter, half a pound
White wine, underlined
Who were you cooking for
With every word so kind

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's plan
I'm stirring in the leeks now
Guessing who you are

[Bridge - sax solo]
Steam on the window
Mussels open one by one

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's meal
I set a second plate down
Just to see how it would feel

[Outro - electric piano fade]
Fold it up, back in the pocket
Someone's dinner, kept

tracks.title: Fourteen Across
tracks.subject: four regulars at a Norwich pub stuck all week on 14 across of the Saturday cryptic crossword, until the landlady pulling pints solves it without looking up
tracks.caption: Barbershop quartet, classic four-part close harmony. Tenor, lead, baritone and bass singing ringing locked chords, the bass with bom-bom pickups, finger snaps on the backbeat, an old upright pub piano only in the intro. Warm close-mic pub-room sound with natural reverb and tightly tuned chords. Male quartet, the lead carrying the melody, tenor floating above. 112 BPM, B-flat major. Jolly, cheeky and triumphant. No drums, no autotune, no pop production, no rap, no solo diva runs.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - pub piano then quartet hum]

[Verse 1]
Saturday the paper came
Four of us, the same old game
Pens out, pints poured, off we go
Thirteen down, a cinch, you know

[Pre-Chorus]
Fourteen across, eight letters, oh
Seven words of clue, and no

[Chorus]
Fourteen across, we're lost
Sunday, Monday, gone
Fourteen across, the cost
Is a pint for every one

[Verse 2]
Tuesday Bill rang up his son
Wednesday Ken asked everyone
Thursday Reg wrote it in pen
Wrong, so we began again

[Chorus]
Fourteen across, we're lost
Friday, still a blank
Fourteen across, the cost
Is filling Maureen's bank

[Bridge - bass bom-bom]
Then Maureen, pulling a pint
Never even looks

[Chorus]
Fourteen across, she's right
Spells it slow and calm
Fourteen across tonight
We're buying Maureen's round

[Outro - ringing tag chord]
Next Saturday, the paper's due
Maureen, there's a pen for you

Warm mono-style room sound with slight tape echo and a close harmony stack. Male high tenor lead, earnest crooning with a soft falsetto break. 76 BPM, E-flat major. Sweet, shy and lightly comic. No trap beats, no autotune, no EDM, no modern R&B runs, no rock guitars.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - doo-wop harmonies, piano triplets, brushed drums]

[Verse 1]
每天早上七點四十
第三個閘門嗶不過
紅燈一亮我就臉紅
後面排了一條長龍

[Pre-Chorus]
穿制服的妳走過來
一刷就讓我過去

[Chorus]
嗶不過的閘門
每天都等我出糗
嗶不過的閘門
讓我多看妳一眼

[Verse 2]
後來妳乾脆站在旁邊
我還沒到妳就笑了
妳說這張卡該換了
我說再等一等

[Bridge - sax solo then harmonies]
今天我買了新的卡
嗶一聲就過了
可是我又走回來
站在妳的窗口前

[Chorus]
嗶不過的閘門
今天輪到我說話
新的卡在我口袋
我想問妳幾點下班

[Outro - harmonies hum, piano triplets fade]
